A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A and B. Content can be matched reliably across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original randomized human-subject experiments involving 600 participants and 30,000 responses across three classification tasks, including model metrics and statistical analyses of human performance.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results, including the model comparisons in Table 1 and human-performance analyses in Table 2.

M1.justification: The classifiers, average-k procedure, marginal and Mondrian conformal prediction, and RAPS/SAPS score functions are unchanged. Equation edits clarify notation without changing prediction procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use FACET occupation classification grouped by age, BiosBias occupation classification grouped by gender, and RAVDESS emotion recognition grouped by gender. No datasets, populations, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Each task retains the same four treatments: unassisted control, average-k, marginal conformal prediction, and conditional Mondrian conformal prediction. Comparator membership in the reported experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The splits, preprocessing, models, tuned hyperparameters, 90% target coverage, and 50 tuning iterations are unchanged. Both versions report 600 participants, 50 per task-treatment combination, with 20 practice trials and 50 analyzed trials per participant.

E4.justification: Figures 4 and 5 retain the analyses of coverage, adoption, set size, singleton frequency, and group difficulty. The new Yule-effects warning is a discussion caveat, not an additional robustness test or analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same GEE analysis, empirical standard-error estimation, and 5%/10% significance annotations in Table 2. Appendix B retains the same ten fixed trial-sampling seeds; no new uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Matched tables and result figures retain the same numerical values and findings. For example, Table 2 reports FACET maximum odds-ratio ratios of 1.26 for marginal and 1.51 for conditional prediction in both versions. Added explanatory notation does not introduce new outcomes.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 replaces the explicit calibration/test exchangeability requirement with a same-distribution statement and removes the exchangeability qualification from the coverage guarantee. This changes the stated assumption and reduces its precision. Other equation edits are notational; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that prediction sets can cause disparate impact, equalizing coverage can worsen it, and equalizing set size or singleton frequency is preferable. The abstract's replacement of general fairness wording with 'disparate impact' aligns with the existing operational definition rather than changing the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 newly warns that group-conditional modifications, including equalizing singleton frequency, are susceptible to Yule effects. This qualifies the recommendation; the existing mechanism explanation and limitations concerning statistical power and classification-only experiments remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The new Reproducibility Statement explicitly reports release of the collected study data alongside code and explains support for reproducing splits, set prediction, and statistical analysis. v1 already linked the same code repository in Appendix A. Hardware, processing instructions, and hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ruggieri et al., 'Can We Trust Fair-AI?', to support the Yule-effects caveat in Section 6.2. The related-work section and the paper's broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract, makes localized terminology and notation edits, and updates the publication header. It moves the existing ethics discussion from Appendix B before the acknowledgments, adds an ICLR ethics statement and a Reproducibility Statement, while preserving the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adds explicit dataset panel headings and Treatment axis labels, with an Equation 7 reference in its caption. Existing figures and tables are retained, with limited resizing and reflow, including Table 7 moving from page 17 to page 18.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency through its explicit study-data release statement and qualifies its fairness recommendation with the Yule-effects caveat. These gains are limited because v1 already supplied detailed appendices and the empirical evidence is unchanged. They are partly offset by the less precise replacement of exchangeability with same-distribution wording in Section 2.1.
